commitResults.messageTitle: level-0: rename chatbot to Joey. add greetings and exit
Added print statements for marked and unmarked tasks
Level-4: Add ToDo, Deadline and Event task types

commitResults.messageBody:
The main method was ~70 lines and mixed multiple abstraction levels:
setup, IO loop, command parsing, task creation, and output formatting all
lived in one long if/else chain. This violated the Single Level of
Abstraction Principle (SLAP) and the "keep functions short" guideline
from the CS2113 code quality notes, making the top-level flow hard to
read and each branch hard to test in isolation.

This change is a pure structural refactor (no behaviour changes,
verified by running the same command sequence and diffing output):

- Extract each command branch into a dedicated private method
  (printList, markTask, unmarkTask, addTypedTask, addGenericTask) and
  the greeting/farewell blocks into printWelcome/printGoodbye.
- Introduce a handleCommand dispatcher so main is now a small loop
  that only decides between "quit" and "delegate".
- Promote the previously-local banner and separator strings to
  class-level constants (BANNER, LINE) so all handlers share one
  source of truth for the UI chrome.
- Promote the tasks array and count to static fields since multiple
  handlers now share them. A future refactor should encapsulate them
  in a TaskList class; keeping them static here is the minimum change
  needed to enable the extraction without expanding scope.
- Drop the trivial "build a scanner object" comment; the code is
  self-explanatory.

Legacy behaviour (the untyped "added: <command>" fallback) is
intentionally preserved to keep this commit a pure refactor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Handle empty todo and unknown commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce JoeyException as a dedicated checked exception for
user-facing input errors. This lets one catch block in the command
dispatcher handle every kind of user mistake uniformly, without
each command handler needing its own error-printing code.

Two error cases are now handled instead of crashing the program:
- 'todo' with no description (or only whitespace) reports a
  friendly message and returns to the prompt.
- Any unrecognised keyword (e.g. 'blah') is now rejected with
  a message instead of being silently stored as an untyped Task.

Also removes the now-unused addGenericTask method, which was
legacy behaviour from an earlier level; the default branch of
the dispatcher throws JoeyException instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Handle malformed deadline and event input
commitResults.messageBody:
Both the deadline and event branches of createTask blindly assumed
their marker keywords ('/by' for deadline; '/from' and '/to' for
event) were present and had non-empty text on both sides. Any
missing piece caused a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, and a
subtler event bug allowed '/to' to appear before '/from', making
substring throw because start > end.

Deadline now validates:
- '/by' marker is present
- description before '/by' is non-empty
- deadline text after '/by' is non-empty

Event now validates:
- '/from' marker is present
- '/to' marker is present
- '/from' appears before '/to'
- description before '/from' is non-empty
- start time between '/from' and '/to' is non-empty
- end time after '/to' is non-empty

Each check throws JoeyException with a message that names the
specific missing piece so the user knows exactly what to fix.
Ordering is deliberate: position checks run before any substring
call so the guard beats the crash, emptiness checks run after
the substrings compute their values. Handled by the existing
catch block in handleCommand, so no dispatcher changes needed.

The mark and unmark commands did zero validation on their argument.
Four different inputs each caused a distinct runtime crash:
- 'mark' alone: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on words[1]
- 'mark abc': NumberFormatException from Integer.parseInt
- 'mark 0' or 'mark -1': ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on tasks[]
- 'mark 99' when list is smaller: NullPointerException on an
  empty slot

Introduce a parseTaskIndex helper that both cases share. It
performs all four checks in order and returns a validated
zero-based index, throwing JoeyException with a specific message
for each failure mode. The helper's placement (before either
markTask or unmarkTask runs) means those two methods stay
focused on their single responsibility of flipping isDone and
printing the confirmation, and none of the validation logic is
duplicated between them.

NumberFormatException is caught inside the helper and rethrown
as JoeyException so all user-facing errors continue to funnel
through the single catch block in handleCommand. The upper
bound uses count rather than MAX_TASKS so users are told 'no
task with that number' rather than being allowed to reference
uninitialised slots.

Move every class from the flat src/main/java root into a proper
Java package structure so the codebase has clear organisation
as it grows:

- seedu.joey        contains Joey (entry point) and JoeyException
                    (the single user-facing exception type)
- seedu.joey.task   contains the Task hierarchy (Task, Todo,
                    Deadline, Event) which form a cohesive
                    domain model

The seedu.joey prefix follows the NUS iP convention (reverse-
domain naming ensures the package is globally unique on any
classpath). Grouping the Task subclasses under a task subpackage
keeps the root uncluttered and signals that those four classes
form one logical unit. JoeyException stays alongside Joey rather
than getting its own single-class subpackage; a seedu.joey.exception
package can be extracted later if more exception types appear.

Each moved file also had its package declaration promoted to
line 1 so the class Javadoc is attached to the class rather than
being silently discarded as package documentation.

Add .vscode/settings.json declaring src/main/java as the Java
source path, so the VS Code Java language server correctly
resolves package names for the new layout instead of expecting
files to sit in the default (unnamed) package.

File moves are done with 'git mv' so history follows the files
via 'git log --follow'.
